summary.intent: Address code review issues in attach.go/attach_test.go, then clean up the branch history by squashing ~38 commits into ~4 clean, descriptive commits rebased onto origin/main.
summary.outcome: All review issues fixed (trailer heuristic, silent error, debug logging, tt:=tt removal), pre-existing lint issues resolved via refactoring, and 38 commits squashed into 4 clean commits with verified identical diff.

repo: The project uses `mise run test:ci` for the full CI test suite (unit, integration, E2E canary).
AgentType is defined in the `types` package, not the `agent` package — `agent.AgentTypeGemini` is a const, not a type.
The `transcript` package import was shadowed by a parameter named `transcript` in writeTranscript/TruncateTranscriptAtUUID — fixed by renaming param to `lines`.
Pre-existing lint issues: `maintidx` (runAttach complexity) and `wrapcheck` (bare json.MarshalIndent error) were unaddressed before this session.
The revive linter flags `indent-error-flow` and builtin shadowing (named return `new`).
Local merge-base diff includes merged-in main changes; the true PR diff is only 5 files — always use `gh pr diff` or `origin/main` as the rebase target to identify actual PR changes.

code.finding: appendCheckpointTrailer used loose strings.Contains(_, ": ") which false-positives on body text like 'connection refused'; replaced with isTrailerLine() regex ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*: (no space before colon).
OpenRepository failure was silently ignored (checked repoErr == nil inline); changed to explicit error return 'failed to open repository'.
detectAgentByTranscript had no logging on failed agent attempts; added logging.Debug per attempt.
json.MarshalIndent error was returned bare (wrapcheck violation); wrapped with fmt.Errorf('failed to re-serialize transcript: %w', err).

runAttach had high cyclomatic complexity (maintidx violation); extracted 5 helpers: validateAttachPreconditions, resolveAgentAndTranscript, collectFileChanges, storeTranscript, printAttachConfirmation.
tt := tt loop variable capture was unnecessary in Go 1.22+ which scopes loop vars per iteration; removed.

workflow: git stash pop can revert staged changes if there are conflicts — verify working tree state after stash operations before assuming changes survived.
For verifying pre-existing lint issues, stash changes and run linter on the base state, but be careful that stash pop failures silently revert code.
When rebasing a long-lived branch, use `gh pr view --json files` to identify the true PR file set rather than diffing against local merge-base (which includes merged-in upstream commits).
Soft-reset + unstage + selective staging is the practical substitute for interactive rebase when -i is unavailable.
Save a diff checksum (md5/sha) before any history rewrite to verify the final state is byte-for-byte identical.
Create a backup branch before any destructive history rewrite (soft reset, rebase).
Go 1.22+ scopes loop variables per iteration, making `tt := tt` captures in table-driven tests unnecessary.

friction: git stash pop failed due to test file conflict, silently reverting all changes in attach.go — required re-applying all edits from scratch.
Interactive rebase (-i flag) is not available, requiring the manual soft-reset + unstage + selective-stage approach for commit squashing.
Initial rebase attempt used local merge-base which included ~85 commits worth of merged-in main changes, causing confusion about which files actually belonged to the PR.
Named return variable `new` shadowed the Go builtin — caught by linter after refactor, required renaming.
agent.AgentType does not exist as a type (only types.AgentType does) — caused a compile error after refactoring storeTranscript's function signature.
open_items: Backup branch `attach-session-id-backup` still exists locally and should be deleted once the PR is merged.
The PR has not been force-pushed with the clean history — the squashed commits are local only; a force-push is needed to update the remote branch.
